cards.front: Recall a key point about Geological Time & Stratigraphy
cards.back: The geological timescale divides Earth's 4.6 billion year history into eons, eras, periods and epochs

cards.front: Recall a key point about Geological Time & Stratigraphy
cards.back: Principle of superposition: in undisturbed sequences, the oldest rocks are at the bottom and youngest at the top

cards.front: Recall a key point about Geological Time & Stratigraphy
cards.back: Principle of original horizontality: sedimentary rocks are deposited horizontally; tilting indicates later deformation

cards.front: Recall a key point about Geological Time & Stratigraphy
cards.back: Principle of cross-cutting relationships: a feature that cuts another is younger than what it cuts

cards.front: Recall a key point about Geological Time & Stratigraphy
cards.back: Relative dating puts rocks in order of age; absolute (radiometric) dating gives a numerical age in millions of years

cards.front: Recall a key point about Geological Time & Stratigraphy
cards.back: Index fossils are organisms that lived for a short time but were widely distributed, used to correlate rock layers across regions

cards.front: What should you know about gcse geology exam tips — geological time & stratigraphy?
cards.back: 1. For Geological Time & Stratigraphy questions, use correct geological terminology and classify features precisely 2. Reference specific geological time periods and processes 3.
